Confirmed instead by: (1) the sealed option chain, where the 2026-10-30 front expiry carries 214% ATM IV and a 12.64% straddle at one day to expiry, which only an event before that expiry explains; (2) four independent third-party sources dated 10-26 to 10-29 naming Thursday 2026-10-29 after the close (TIKR 10-26, QuiverQuant 10-26, Yahoo/StockStory 10-27, MarketBeat; MarketScreener calendar); (3) the company's own 8-K of 2026-10-05, which keeps the outgoing CFO as principal financial officer through exactly 2026-10-30, consistent with a 10-29 print. Session amc per every source and the company's history; MarketBeat gives a 5:30 PM ET call, against the usual 1:30 PM PT.
conviction_note: abs_move 12.5 (straddle 12.64, median prior reaction 10.31, guide-driven name whose last four reactions were 6.9-21.8 pts) times a 54% p_up gives +1.0; the findings sum to +1.2. A likely revenue beat (the company beat its own guide midpoint by 4.9% and 3.2% in the last two quarters) and an easy tariff-hit Q4 2025 comp lean the Q4 guide up. Against that: Europe's cross-border-retailer headwind persists, Alphabet's YouTube/Search deceleration landed last night, and a CFO three days into the job gives the first guide. The name sold a 2.7% revenue beat for -8.7% in August, so p_up stays close to 50.

findings.finding: Pinterest has beaten the midpoint of its own revenue guide by a widening margin in both 2026 quarters. Q1: $1,008m against a $951-971m guide (+4.9% vs midpoint, +3.8% vs top). Q2: $1,180m against $1,133-1,153m (+3.2% vs midpoint, +2.3% vs top). The Q3 consensus of $1.20-1.21bn sits at the midpoint-to-top of the $1,190-1,210m guide, so a repeat of even the smaller Q2 overshoot gives ~$1.235-1.24bn, about 2-3% above the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: revenue beat consensus by 2.73% and adj. EPS by 20%, stock -8.68% on a Q3 guide ~1.9% below consensus. May 2026: Q1 beat plus a Q2 guide ~2% above consensus, +6.86%. Nov 2025: revenue in line, weak guide, -21.76%. The reported-quarter beat has not set the sign on any of the last three prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits at the guide rather than at the guide plus the company's demonstrated overshoot. If the street had priced the pattern, the published Q3 revenue estimate would be ~$1.23bn+ rather than $1.20-1.21bn, and previews would not note that 'a result at the low end of the guided ranges would miss.' Analysts have kept estimates unchanged for 30 days (Yahoo/StockStory 10-27). Buy-side whisper numbers likely carry part of it.
findings.independence: Q1 overshoot from a separate document, the Q1 2026 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001506293/000150629326000066/q1-26xpressrelease.htm (Q2 guide $1,133-1,153m) and the Q4 2025 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1506293/000150629326000019/q4-25xpressrelease.htm (Q1 guide $951-971m). Same company, same habit, two quarters.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide, the line this stock trades on, laps an easy comparison. Q4 2025 revenue grew only 14% (13% constant currency) after the then-CFO said larger US retailers were cutting ad spend under tariff margin pressure, with home-furnishings tariffs adding to it. US & Canada grew just 9% in Q3 2025, then re-accelerated to +13% in Q1 2026 and +18% in Q2 2026. On two-year stacks the August Q3 guide (14% midpoint on a 17% comp) is ~31 points, while the Q4 consensus (~$1.52bn, ~15% on a 14% comp) is only ~29. A Q4 guide on the Q3 guide's stack would be ~17%, about $1.54bn, ~1.5% above consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide has set the sign on every recent print. May 2026: guide ~2% above consensus, +6.86%. August 2026: guide ~1.9% below consensus, -8.68%. Nov 2025: Q4 guide midpoint below consensus, -21.76%. Feb 2026: guide below consensus, -16.83%. So roughly 4-8 points per 2% of guide surprise.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market priced the easy comp, Q4 consensus would sit above 15% growth, previews would frame the Q4 guide as a likely beat, and the stock would not have slid 10.8% in five sessions into the print. The TIKR preview (10-26) treats a Q4 guide above ~$1.52bn as the bull case rather than the base case.
findings.independence: Tariff cause of the weak Q4 2025: TIKR/Barchart coverage of the Nov 2025 call quoting the CFO on 'larger US retailers navigate tariff-related margin pressure', https://www.tikr.com/blog/pinterest-nyse-pins-stock-plunges-over-19-on-q3-earnings-miss-and-weak-forecast. US&C re-acceleration: Q1 and Q2 2026 8-Ks. This is an inference from company numbers; management has not said it.

findings.finding: Europe's headwind does not lap before Q4. The EU replaced the €150 duty exemption with a flat €3-per-item duty on 1 July 2026, and a further handling fee of roughly €2 a parcel is due by 1 November 2026. Ahead of the duty Temu roughly halved and Shein nearly ended their European Google Shopping presence from March. On the Q2 call the CFO said this pressure from Asia-based cross-border retailers continued into Q3. Europe slowed from +27% (Q1) to +12% (Q2) and laps a +41% Q3 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 guide that carried this headwind was cut below consensus and the stock fell 8.68% in August 2026. No prior quarter isolates Europe alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced for Q3, because management flagged it in August. What may not be priced is persistence into Q4, plus the second fee from 1 November. If it were priced, the Q4 consensus would show a Europe deceleration, but that consensus (~15%) does not separate regions. Net of the rest of the company: Europe is ~18% of revenue ($213m of $1,180m in Q2) against US&C at 75% growing 18%, so a 5-point Europe shortfall is under 1 point of total growth.
findings.independence: CFO comment on continuing Q3 pressure from Q2 call summaries (Yahoo Q2 2026 call summary, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/pinterest-inc-q2-2026-earnings-123000649.html). EU duty start: Euronews 2026-07-01, https://www.euronews.com/2026/07/01/eu-slaps-3-duty-fee-on-shein-temu-and-aliexpress-imports. Europe growth: Q1/Q2 2026 8-Ks.

findings.finding: Meta's Q3 2026 results (10-21) show strong performance-ad demand in the quarter Pinterest is reporting: advertising revenue $63.06bn vs $50.08bn (+26%), ad impressions +10%, average price per ad +14%, and a Q4 revenue guide of $73-76bn with the midpoint above consensus. Meta is the closest competitor for Pinterest's lower-funnel shopping budgets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline series on peer read-throughs. In August 2026 Pinterest fell 8.68% on its own guide despite a strong ad tape. Meta fell ~7% on its own print (capex and costs), so peer strength has not translated into stock strength this season.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Pinterest rose ~11.9% over the month to 10-27 (Yahoo/StockStory), then gave most of it back. The read-through lands on Q3 revenue and the Q4 guide, while Pinterest's own consensus stayed unchanged for 30 days. If the market had carried it into estimates, the Q3 revenue consensus would have moved above the guide's top.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a direct counterparty. Alphabet's same-quarter print points the other way (next finding). Deutsche Bank was cited in search-result text as saying digital ad spend ran stronger than expected through Q3, but that was unverified and has no URL, so it is not used.

findings.finding: Alphabet's Q3 2026 release (10-28, after the close) shows Google's ad lines decelerating. Search & other $63.35bn vs $56.57bn (+12%, from +17% in Q2). YouTube ads $11.21bn vs $10.26bn (+9%, from +13% in Q2). Network +1%. Total Google advertising +11% vs +14.5% in Q2. GOOGL fell ~10% after hours on a profit miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline. Historically Pinterest has traded in sympathy with Alphabet's ad revenue surprises, for example +4.5% on an Alphabet ad beat in April 2025 (Reuters via iTiger), but that is a 2025 example.
findings.why_not_priced: Released the evening before. Pinterest's seal at 17:12 UTC on 10-29 ($20.445) already reflects one session of it, so this is largely in the price by the entry. What remains is whether YouTube's brand/upper-funnel slowdown shows up in Pinterest's Q4 guide.
findings.independence: Proxy. Points the opposite way to the Meta finding. Pinterest's ads are lower-funnel and shopping-led (Performance+ is 30% of lower-funnel revenue per the CEO at Goldman, per TIKR 10-26), closer to Meta than to YouTube.

findings.finding: James Dibbo became CFO on 2026-10-26, three days before the print. He was VP and CFO of Amazon's Global Entertainment, Advertising and Corporate Development. Julia Brau Donnelly, who resigned 2026-08-26 'to pursue another opportunity' with no disagreement, remains principal financial officer through 2026-10-30. The Q4 guide is the first given on a new CFO's watch, which raises the risk of a conservative reset or a changed guidance framework.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CFO-transition print for this company in the baseline. The stock fell ~5-6% on 10-26, the day Dibbo started; QuiverQuant attributes it partly to the transition.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced in the 10-26 drop. The guide-setting risk is not in the published Q4 consensus. If the market expected a reset, the Q4 consensus would have been trimmed; instead estimates stayed flat for 30 days. The new CFO's $9m+ RSU package includes relative-TSR performance shares, which would favour a beatable first guide.
findings.independence: Departure 8-K 2026-08-26, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1506293/000150629326000117/pins-20260826.htm (no disagreement). QuiverQuant 10-26, https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Pinterest+shares+slide+as+investors+position+ahead+of+earnings+and+absorb+CFO+transition (AI-generated attribution). Inference on how a new CFO guides; no document says it.

findings.finding: Positioning was de-risked into the print. The stock fell from $22.32 (10-23) to $20.445 at the seal (-10.84% over 5 sessions) with no company-specific negative. The sealed skew is -10.65 vol points (calls bid over puts) and put/call OI is 0.52. Short interest rose to 9.10% of float (3.8 days to cover) at 10-15. The stock sits near the $18.17 average price of the company's $2bn H1 2026 buyback and below Elliott's $22.72 conversion price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pinterest fell after 4 of its last 5 prints (TIKR). The one rise, May 2026 +6.86%, followed a guide above consensus. No sourced series on reactions after a pre-print drawdown.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is not unpriced information. It lowers the bar for the guide line and gives a modest squeeze mechanism (9% of float short) on an in-line-or-better guide. If holders were still positioned for a beat, the 5-day run-up would be positive and the skew neutral.
findings.independence: Skew and run-up from the sealed baseline. The drop's lack of company news per QuiverQuant 10-26 (shares the CFO-finding source).

findings.finding: Capital return capacity is large against the market cap and was barely used in Q2. $1,948m remained under the March 2026 authorization at June 30, about 17% of a ~$11.6bn market cap (566.3m shares at $20.45). Q2 repurchases were only $78.6m after ~$1.95bn in Q1. FCF runs ~$270m a quarter. On 10-15 the company upsized its undrawn revolver from $500m to $700m (5 years, SOFR+1.25%, nothing outstanding, in covenant compliance). An accelerated or newly sized buyback alongside the print is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: March 2026: the Elliott $1bn convert funding a $3.5bn buyback authorization, about +9% premarket (BNN Bloomberg 2026-03-03). No baseline print carried a buyback-only surprise.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing has been announced. With the stock back near its H1 buyback average and below the convert price, an accelerated repurchase would be new information. The revolver is financing: it was asked what it buys, and the answer is an upsized backstop with no draw and no distress signal (Lesson 4), so its sign is zero to positive.

findings.finding: Q3 MAU looks likely to beat the ~653m consensus. Q3 has been the seasonally strong quarter (Q2-to-Q3 2025 went 578m to 600m, +22m), Q2 2026 was 640m (+11% y/y), and 640m plus a repeat seasonal add gives ~660m. The 653m consensus implies growth slowing to ~8.8% from 11%. A single source carries that consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Record MAU in Q2 2026 (640m, +11%) did not stop the August -8.68%. User beats have not set the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus figure (GuruFocus preview, https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9147239/pinterest-q3-earnings-on-deck-what-to-expect, snippet only, the page returned 403) sits below a simple seasonal extrapolation. If priced, the consensus would read ~660m. US&C MAU growth is only +4%, so the beat would be in the low-ARPU Rest of World.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 MAU from the Q2 8-K. Bar is single-source, so capped small.

findings.finding: Pinterest's business-community forum carries many June-August 2026 threads from creators and advertisers reporting sudden drops in impressions and outbound clicks (e.g., 'Massive drop in impressions with no explanation'), alongside continuing complaints about AI-generated content and automated moderation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. The 2025 ban/AI-slop episode coincided with record MAU and no visible revenue effect.
findings.why_not_priced: Anecdotal and creator-side. Lower outbound clicks for publishers can coincide with more on-platform shopping engagement, so the sign for revenue is unclear. A broad series (company MAU +11%) contradicts any user exodus.
findings.independence: Gigazine 2026-02-24, https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20260224-pinterest-ai-slop (complaints, not data). No systematic measurement.

outside_window.finding: On 2026-09-30 the board amended the Level-21 severance and change-in-control plan. After a change in control, a qualifying termination now pays the greater of the target bonus or the bonus earned on actual performance, and single-trigger vesting applies only if awards are not assumed. This comes with Elliott as largest holder holding a board seat, and some commentary speculates about a sale. It is a sale-optionality fact with no dated catalyst inside the window.

The EU's ~€2 per-parcel handling fee on low-value imports is due by 2026-11-01. It extends the Asia cross-border retailer headwind in Europe past the window. Its in-window effect is folded into the Europe finding.

baseline_tension: The net lean is mildly positive and agrees with the skew (-10.65, upside paid), which suggests part of it is already priced. It cuts against the 5-day run-up of -10.84%, which says holders de-risked, and against a 4-of-5 record of falling after prints. That record is why p_up stays at 54 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold a 2.7% revenue beat for -8.7%): guide-overshoot finding +0.5 to +0.3, MAU finding +0.3 to +0.2, p_up 55 to 54, print_vs_bar 3.0 to 2.5

Lesson 5 (proxy and inference smaller; unexplained drawdown worth 0): Q4 two-year-stack inference +1.5 to +1.0; Meta read-through +0.6 to +0.4; positioning finding +0.8 to +0.4, since it partly rests on a drop with no company cause; forum anecdotes -0.2 to -0.1 against the broad MAU series
Lesson 7 (sign against skew; short interest checked, 9.1% float, not crowded): negatives running against an upside-paid skew shrunk, CFO -0.7 to -0.5, Alphabet -0.6 to -0.5
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): Europe -0.8 to -0.6, net of US&C (75% of revenue, +18%)

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the 10-15 revolver was asked what it buys, found to be an undrawn upsized backstop, and signed zero-to-positive inside the capital-return finding, not as a negative

Lesson 6 (bar and window): the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimates. The CIC-plan amendment and EU handling fee were kept in outside_window. The Q4 and MAU consensus are single-source, so the findings that depend on them stay small
